title: Find the Smallest Balanced Index
summary: Given an integer array, find the smallest index where the sum of elements to the left equals the product of elements to the right.
statement: Given an integer array, find the smallest index where the sum of elements to the left equals the product of elements to the right. If no such index exists, return -1.
constraints: nums is a nonempty array of positive integers.
At index i, compare the sum strictly left of i with the product strictly right of i; an empty product is one.
Return the smallest balanced index or -1.
reference_solution:
def smallest_balanced_index(nums):
    left_sum=sum(nums);right_product=1
    for index in range(len(nums)-1,-1,-1):
        left_sum-=nums[index]
        if left_sum==right_product:return index
        right_product*=nums[index]
        if right_product>=left_sum:break
    return -1

def smallest_balanced_index(nums):
    left_sum=sum(nums);right_product=1
    for index in range(len(nums)-1,-1,-1):
        left_sum-=nums[index]
        if left_sum==right_product:return len(nums)-1-index
        right_product*=nums[index]
        if right_product>=left_sum:break
    return -1
hints: Scan from right to left while maintaining the sum to the left and product to the right.
Remove the current value from the total before comparing, then multiply it into the suffix after comparing.
With positive values, once the suffix product is at least the left sum, moving left cannot restore equality.
The invariants give the exact two sides at every index; positivity makes the early stop safe and also makes a balanced index unique.

tests.explanation: At index one, the left sum two equals the right product two.
The empty left sum is zero and empty right product is one, so no index is balanced.
